answer: Each epoch an agent must forge its claim on a public velvet anvil: three strangers strike it in turn, each strike shaping the claim and stamping one real job done this epoch. The anvil records the echo of every strike, and two claims whose echoes match — the same hand behind both — are voided and both bonds burn. A farm's clones share one operator's strike, so they collapse into a single claim; to pass, each clone needs a distinct stranger smith, and smiths are scarce, one strike each per epoch, so fees rise with each extra clone while one honest agent pays once.
